binder_expression_surface.coverage_argument: the goal predicate is a conjunction over goal_files content and goal_language selection (+ optional override flag); each clause has exactly one route from a given initial world, so the 3 x 4 route grid covers every conjunction the binder can express on a single path
binder_expression_surface.not_covered: anything needing a second action target (T3), a second transformation of one file (T1), or an inter-member evidence channel (T2) -- each reported with its own witness above

T1_serial_handoff.spec: create a file, then patch the freshly created content
T1_serial_handoff.why: workspace.create binds content = task.goal_files[main_path], so the created file is already at its goal state and workspace.apply_patch then refuses with 'file already at goal state'

scripted_steps.failure: bind_failure: file already at goal state

T1_serial_handoff.consequence: the earlier create_then_patch surface is a create-only task, which is why member-c solves it alone; a serial-handoff structure needs a binder change, not a composition change

T3_dual_goal_two_files.spec: two independent files, one needing an override and one needing a patch
T3_dual_goal_two_files.why: _bind resolves every action kind against task.main_path, so no action can ever target the second goal path; its content clause can be pre-satisfied in initial_files but its language clause cannot
T3_dual_goal_two_files.note: the expressible reading of 'jointly required' is one file with two clauses, which is the patch x * row of the grid -- and member-d covers it alone.  The grid is therefore the closest admissible substitute.

t2_member_input_surface.why: predict_episode takes one argument, and every element of the tuple passed to it is the same tensor object repeated -- so the only per-call variation is the member's own history length.  No member is ever handed another member's failure, so 'B reads A's failure evidence' cannot be built out of task design
t2_member_input_surface.consequence: M4 does carry that failure information, but in the composition layer (it reads the step list), not in any member -- which is why M4 is a rule change while T2 would be a capability change
